utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Cvoro. Please continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvoro. Yesterday at page 3093 -- excuse me, 30929, I believe, yeah, you spoke about the establishment of the SRNA news agency, and in particular focusing on Mr. Todor Dutina and his efforts. I just wanted to clarify one thing about SRNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that respect and I'd like to call up 65 ter 17412.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You'll see before you in Serbian, and in a moment the Court should see in English, the decision on the forming of the Serb news agency SRNA, and I'm not sure why we're not seeing the English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's no English translation in e-court, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on quickly to a couple of other topics and we'll return when the English has been uploaded so that the Court can also see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You stated in your witness statement at paragraph 15 that -- you mention the Catholic church in the centre of Pale which was preserved that day and then stated that there was never a mosque in Pale.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a single mosque in Pale; however, there was another mosque or there was a mosque some 10 kilometres away from Pale. So in Pale itself there was no mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. So in fact, Mr. Cvoro, there were three -- at least three mosques in Pale municipality, all of which --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- all of which were destroyed or damaged during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that respect I'd like to turn, please, to 65 ter 13853B. Your Honours and counsel, this is an excerpt from P04070, and specifically from pages 205 through 210 of that exhibit, which is a broader exhibit referring to mosques around RS territory. But for ease of reference and for purposes of more easily showing it in court, we've created a separate exhibit number. That's shown on the screen. I'd like to turn first to the first page, and if we can see those two photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This depicts the mosque at Praca, both before --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prace.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Prace, thank you, sir, before and after. If we could turn to page 2 of the e-court, we'll see the mosque at Podvitez which was also destroyed, and finally, on page 3, the mosque at Bogovici which was also destroyed. So, in fact, Mr. Cvoro, the reference in page 15 to never having been a mosque in Pale is a limited reference to the centre of Pale, that is, Pale town, and does not reflect the fact that three mosques in Pale municipality not only existed but were destroyed. You're nodding your head "yes." You just have to answer audibly "yes" if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you are correct. These mosques indeed existed in the territory of Pale municipality. They were preserved as long as I was in power and while the Muslim population was still present. I don't know what happened later on. I do know that in Prace there was a separation line there and there was combat. Now, whether it was destroyed under those circumstances or later on, that's something I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'll tender that 65 ter number, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder why do we need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's true it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- admit it separately --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think you're right about that. The purpose was to be able to more easily show it to the Court and it obviously exists in P4070, so you're quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could quickly return to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I only briefly. My objection stands. We have no proof that, for example, the first photograph was taken from the same place about the same place. We see a dome on one end of the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and some trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for you to intervene at this time, Mr. Karadzic. Let's continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, I began our session today by asking you about SRNA. We called up the Official Gazette in the Serbian language, didn't have the English; we have that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So if we could call up 17412 we'll see both the Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I mentioned, this arose because of your brief discussion about the establishment of SRNA and the focus on Mr. Dutina, and I simply wanted to establish, as we see here, that SRNA was established by the authorities of Republika Srpska and was funded from the budget of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is. I assisted the news agency SRNA financially and I've already explained how and in what way. In other words, I found premises for their operation and I provided the minimum amount needed for the SRNA agency to become operational. I had no authority to establish it and it was not part of the remit of municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I tender 17412 , Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 17412 becomes Exhibit P6032, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, in paragraph 14 of your statement you mention what you refer to as the Muslim municipality of Pale which included Renovica and Prace, Prace as you pointed out earlier, and stated if the VRS wanted to take over the Muslim municipality of Pale it could easily have done so, but it did not because the Muslim population was the majority there. And as mentioned, you indicated that the -- this municipality included Renovica and Prace. Those are the two villages you specifically mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to look at 65 ter 23869, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, this is a regular combat report to the Main Staff dated October 14th, 1992. And as we can see in item 2, it relates that: Our units are continuing offensive operations in the Renovica sector and have liberated Renovica. So, in fact, Mr. Cvoro, contrary to the indication in paragraph 14 of your statement, the VRS in fact took over Renovica, notwithstanding the fact, as you relate, that the Muslim population was a majority there, or at least as you said. That's correct, isn't it? And that happened in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say yet again that at the time I was not president of the Executive Council. This order arrived on the 14th of October. As far as I know, Renovica was never fully under control of the VRS. And that the Muslims constituted a majority. In Renovica there was a military barracks, JNA barracks, which is something that the Main Staff must have kept in mind in order to preserve it and draw some resources from there. Renovica is not a village, it's a local commune. 90 per cent of the population in that local commune were Muslims. Part of the Muslim population in Prace or, to be more specific, in the Prace local commune the percentage of Muslims was 80 per cent. It was also partially controlled by federal units or units of the Federation. After a while a separation line was created deep inside the territory of Pale municipality. And after some time, they automatically set up their own municipality which is nowadays called Prace Pale with its seat in Prace.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. It doesn't directly contradict the witness since it wasn't at a time when he was in his position and the time that he was speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, Mr. President, do I really need to respond to that? Just take a look at paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber finds it relevant. We'll receive it. Exhibit P6033.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And -- thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Cvoro, I want to return to where we began our examination with -- and draw your attention to one additional document. And where we began was in connection with questions about those portions of your statement indicating that Muslims left only of their own free will. Now, when I asked you about that yesterday, particularly in connection with the remarks you made at the June 18th, 1992, Municipal Assembly meeting concerning efforts by the police to move Muslims out, you said to the Court: "I guarantee that there was no forced moving out of the Muslims from Pale." That's at transcript pages 30939.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'd like to look at 65 ter 01583.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This, Mr. Cvoro, is a document dated the 7th of July, 1992, sent to the War-Time Board of Commissioners of Pale Municipality and personally to Biljana Plavsic, relating -- and it's signed by you and it relates to certain problems encountered by the Executive Committee. And in paragraph 2, which was written at the time, you relate just the opposite of what you stated yesterday. It says that there was forced and wilful moving out of the Muslim population. And that was the reality of Pale, Mr. Cvoro, wasn't it, that Muslims were forced out?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I meant. After a decision was made by the Assembly, many Muslims had their own interpretation of the Assembly decision, understanding that they had to move out of Pale municipality. That's why many came to see me and the president for clarification, i.e., how and in what way this decision created on the 18th of June should be read. Never does it say that the Muslims were obliged to leave Pale. The Assembly made this decision, stating that every citizen has a constitutional right to choose where he or she wishes to live. There were misinterpretations on the Serb side too, who also thought that the Muslims ought to go, resulting in individuals applying pressure, but that pressure was never exercised by the authorities or anyone else involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't see anything in your statement referring to pressure applied to the Muslims causing them to leave the municipality. You didn't -- now you're saying that there was pressure applied to the Muslims, but that's not in your statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individuals. If such things were done, it was done by individuals, not the authorities; and I was at the helm of those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So your position now, before this Court, is that when you wrote Mrs. Plavsic and said there was forced and wilful moving out of the Muslim population, that referred to actions that you didn't take but that others did, is that it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say others did. I repeat: If it was done, it was done by individuals. We were not pleased with what was going on in the territory of Pale at the time. That is why we sent this document to President Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correction for the transcript. The witness said: We were not happy with the co-operation and not with what was going on, line 14. Probably co-operation of the services rather than goings-on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know what, I would appreciate if the accused would refrain from interpretations offered to the witness while the witness is on the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, now you say to the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, let's clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, please --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Judge asked us both to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Cvoro, if you remember that. What were you not pleased with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were not pleased with wilful interpretations of Assembly decisions by Muslims and individual Serbs. That is why we established contact with the Muslims, or rather, they came to see us seeking an interpretation of the decision. We interpreted the decision as it was proclaimed. My neighbours came to see me from Bogovici and asked me what to do: Was this decision for us to move out or not? I said: It was not a decision that is forcing you to move out; it is your right to decide where you wanted to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Meanwhile --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, so when the answer of the witness is not clear, then it's more appropriate for you to take up that issue in your re-examination instead of intervening during the cross-examination. I think that issue was a bit more than just translation issue. Please bear that in mind. Let's continue, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but it was stated: We were not happy with co-operations. We can go back to the audio recording. I did not want to clarify anything but the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We too suggest that the audio recordings be revisited.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This may affect any further examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, then I would like the CLSS to look into the matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And when I asked you a moment ago about the fact that there was forced moving out of the Muslim population and that it seemed that you were saying that referred to actions taken by others and not you, you said: "I can't say others did." But the fact, Mr. Cvoro, is that you refer to a large number of illegal and criminal actions in your letter to Mrs. Plavsic. That's what you said at the time, that's what you knew at the time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was general crime which appeared and it did not refer to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It referred to actions taken against Muslims. It referred to the forced and wilful moving out of the Muslim population, which - as you said in your letter - created a series of problems including a large number of illegal and criminal actions. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such things existed. On the Serb side there was crime, but as for any significant criminal acts in terms of exercising pressure on the Muslims, well, I don't have any specific examples of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as you did yesterday at transcript pages 30935, 30948, you once again laid the problem at the door-step of the police, complaining that you and the Executive Committee had no authority, no jurisdiction over the police, which had a vertical chain of command. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoro.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have no further questions -- except to tender this document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit P6034. Mr. Karadzic, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, Excellency. But I'm going to start from the last answer that was provided to a question that was highly complex, and I'm going to read it out to the witness so that we determine what this pertains to exactly. So I'm going to read the question, Mr. Cvoro, in English so that it is interpreted more correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] "And as you did yesterday at transcript pages 30935, 30948, you once again laid the problem at the door-step of the police, complaining that you and the Executive Committee had no authority, no jurisdiction over the police, which had a vertical chain of command." [Interpretation] Before that there was another question. [In English] "... action taken against Muslims. It referred to the forced and wilful moving out of the Muslim population which - as you said in your letter - created a series of problems including a large number of illegal and criminal actions; isn't that right?" [Interpretation] I was waiting for the interpretation to finish. So, Mr. Cvoro, what you said in your last response, was that correct, that the police had a vertical chain of command? Does that also mean that you confirmed the existence, or rather, that there were -- there were forcible moves and voluntarily moves or movings out related to the police?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness start his answer again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, you started answering the question while the question itself was being translated. Could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said that the police, otherwise by its structure, has a vertical chain and the local authorities have no authority over the police. But I did not say that the police exerted pressure along this vertical chain against Muslims in the territory of Pale and that they were carrying out forcible expulsions. I only meant the hierarchical organisation of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please clarify a few things. First of all, when was it that you first received a request for -- from someone to move out?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in April, the 9th of April, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the executive respond, and before that, was an Assembly meeting held or did the executive reply on their own?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Executive Board, or rather, the Crisis Staff responded to that request put forth by a group of Muslims, and after a while, when we left -- or rather, when we went to places where there was a majority population of Muslims, when we talked to them, when we could not persuade them to stay on, then, then, we proceeded from the following, that this request should be examined by the highest organ of local authority and that is the Assembly. And the Assembly decided as it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up D31, Serb page 4, English page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This Assembly session where you asked the parliament to state its views, was that held on the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Assembly meeting took place on the 18th of June. The representatives of the Assembly were Assemblymen who were elected multi-party elections. These people had to be assembled because most of them were at positions and in different places elsewhere. They discussed the subject matter for a long time and their decision says that this is a constitutional right to move about freely and to reside at different places freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you leave the -- can you read the paragraph -- no, not in the statement, no. What you see on the screen, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In order to keep the discussion focused, the Assembly propose that a working group formulate a draft decision on the moving out of Muslims and Croats, stressing in it that the departure of these people from the territory of the municipality would be done on a voluntary basis and in an organised manner."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what was it that you decided -- or actually, why didn't the executive go on dealing with this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we handed this authority over to the Assembly because that is the highest organ of authority of the municipality. We no longer had powers in that sense, we were powerless in the face of pressure exerted by Muslims who wanted to leave Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D28, could we please have that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did these pressures start?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the very beginning of the war. I've already said, the 9th of April, when they presented their first requests and all the way up until their departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, this document that you signed, is that a response to that request? When did you sign this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a response to that request. The Muslims had their safety guaranteed in the municipality, but also their vital food supplies were guaranteed. Also all protection was afforded to them like to all other citizens, including health care and so on. There was no reason for them to move out because -- because -- because they had full civic freedoms. Also in paragraph 3, since the SDS and the SDA were the largest political parties in Pale, they were given the possibility of reaching mutual agreement on the problems that had cropped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ban the work of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. They had continuity because telephones were working. They were linked to the telephone exchange and there were no problems whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the SDA also subsidized by the municipal budget?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was, but this budget that was adopted in an emergency situation meant that they had not been planned for one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in the meantime had they not established their own municipality and didn't they have their own budget?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I don't know. They established this municipality Prace Pale. I don't know the exact date, but probably they did have a budget of their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your knowledge, what was the position of the republican authorities in relation to the question of the departure of non-Serbs from Serb territories?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim with full responsibility that I never received any order from any republican organs, the Presidency and the Assembly. What we did, we did with the scope of our own authority, the authority of the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D446, could we have that now, please. In Serbian page 5 and in English page 6. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me assist in order not to call up the first page. This is a session of the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska, the 11th of July, 1992 -- I beg your pardon, government meeting held on the 11th of July. Could you please read paragraph 3 -- actually, could the Serbian version be enlarged a little bit.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A work group has been formed made up of Milan Trbojevic, government deputy prime minister, and the representatives of the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Justice, and the Ministry of Health, Work, Welfare, and Family Affairs to prepare a regulation (platform) on the treatment of Muslims and other nations on the territory of the Serb Republic of BH. In accordance with this, the constitutional rights and obligations, international conventions on civil rights and freedoms that obliges have to be taken into consideration. "A larger debate would have to be held on the proposed document exclusively at the session of the Assembly of the Serb People of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How does this fit in to what you knew about the position of the state organs about this matter?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D27. Third page in this document as it has been admitted. The 24th to the 26th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in terms of the date is what, two months? What?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we proceed. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, can some kind of foundation be laid for the presentation of such documents to the witness. I complained yesterday and I believe that complaint was understood by the Court that this manner of examination is quite leading, particularly in the absence of any foundation that the witness attended a particular session, knew about the issue, was in a position to shed any light on that at all, rather than being led to a particular position by virtue of the presentation of a document outlining it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber absolutely agrees with Mr. Tieger's observation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll do my best to correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, do you remember that the Assembly --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection, objection, that's obviously beginning in a leading fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in July a session of the National Assembly was held in Pale and did you see this in the media? Did you follow this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you quite frankly, I don't know and I didn't really follow this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you have any knowledge as to what my position was in relation to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I and the municipal authorities were never subjected to any kind of pressure from you in respect of the Muslims. I never received any order or any invitation to come and see you and to discuss the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am going to read my words out to you. It's at the very top in Serbian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any point. If it is already in evidence, why do we have to put it to the witness? We have the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, there is a reference to Pale here, which is his municipality. I don't have to read it. I can ask you to read it yourself and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, look at the answer he gave about your position in relation to the Muslims, and he said he never -- he was never subjected to any kind of pressure from you in respect of the Muslims. And you can ask an open question to the witness with respect to others, but reading out this passage from this seems to have no point to me. Why don't you put an open question to the witness first and see what we can get from him further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know percentage-wise how many Muslims there were in the municipality of Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 70 per cent of the population was Serb and about 30 per cent was non-Serb. Now that includes Croats and Muslims and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is what I say in this speech correct, that in July there were 20 per cent of them and that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- no one touched them and that they communicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I think at this point it's very clear that this is not a matter of inexperience or inadvertence; this is a blatant attempt to override the Chamber's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give up. I give up. Even if it is blatant or impudent, that was not the intention. I'm simply not used to this yet. Can we please have D34 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the review of the commission, or rather, you mentioned that you were not happy with the work produced by one commission and then you established another one. Can you please take a look at this document that you signed on the 14th of July, 1992, and can you tell us what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the commissions that worked on the ground in various locations had not adequately recorded the property of the non-Serb population. So we learned that there was abuse and that there had been some misappropriations of property. We did not even adopt all the reports of these commissions, so we decided to establish a review commission whose task was to tour all the areas where Muslims lived and to establish what the actual truthful situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first sentence of this task and the first one further down, can you read it out?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The commission's task is to: "Examine the manner in which the property of citizens who are non-Serbs is being used for each household separately, using the reports compiled by the commissions who were previously in the field." That is the first one. Do you want the second one too?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just the first line of the second one.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Seal off all houses and outbuildings that have been abandoned and have not been transferred by legal contract to" -- I cannot see this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Contracts"?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not "contracts." Yes. "... legal contracts to citizens of Serb ethnicity and nobody has been assigned to protect them from damage."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this done?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of it was done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have P6031 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was suggested to you yesterday that the private property left behind by Muslims was considered war booty. I'd like us now to have a look at what the government had to say in terms of war booty and perhaps you can tell us how much of that property ended up in the budget of the state and municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on para 4, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Commission is required to draw ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll up, please. The left column. Go down now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Commission is required to draw up a record for any transfer of movable property and assets. The record shall contain particulars of the person delivering the goods, the means whereby the said person gained possession of the goods, the quantity and type of goods and/or cash, foreign currency, and valuables, the condition, origin and ownership of the goods, the name and origin of the manufacturer, and any observations regarding the keeping, storage, maintenance, and shelf life of the goods."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go even further down on the page to see where we have a definition of "war booty." Actually, go up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read out Article 1?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All legal entities and natural persons who have acquired, in the course of war operations or by other means, movable property and assets (commodities, technical equipment, vehicles, and equipment) are required to deliver the same immediately or within 24 hours at the latest to the Republic's emergency reserves at the nearest location. "Cash, foreign currency, gold, other precious metals and valuables shall be deposited in the treasury of the National Bank of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this refer to private property such as apartments and other things which were not acquired in combat, including movable property?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Muslims take with them whatever they wanted when they moved to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims from Pale on their request wanted to leave and they did. I cannot accept the assertion that they were driven out. They left with all of their personal belongings as well as motor vehicles. Those who did not have vehicles were put on buses with all of their personal belongings and went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did Serbs leave Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say the following. As for the Serbs who were the first ones to be driven out of Sarajevo, they were from Pofalici. They had to leave while the military operations were still ongoing. They came without any of their possessions to Pale and Han Pijesak. In Pofalici, there were mostly Serbs from the territory of the Romanija plateau. Many of their houses were torched and many were killed --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection. Beyond the scope of cross and, apart from that, tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Can we have D111. Zoom in, please, and we do have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are instructions I signed on the 23rd of August --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me, I don't know if I have to offer the same objection and the same admonition has to be given to Mr. Karadzic every time, but we're back in the same position of the accused presenting documents to the witness before laying any form of foundation. Same objection. It should be taken off the screen and he should be asked to ask questions about what this witness knows and not direct him to information that he wants the witness to affirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, could you have a word with Mr. Karadzic as to the manner in which he conducts re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, you were asked and you stated in the statement that you held back from certifying many kinds of contracts drawn up in war-time conditions. Did you see this instruction on abandoned apartments which I issued and sent to the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm sorry. Could I have a reference to that in the statement because my recollection is almost the opposite of what is stated in the statement, that the witness emphasized that he verified such agreements.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvoro said so during cross-examination. He said that they did not accept gladly to have contracts on the exchange of property certified in courts between Muslims and Serbs because there was a war. It was in cross-examination and I believe it is somewhere in the statement as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I mean, the cross-examination wasn't that long. I'd appreciate the page reference. I imagine there's one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll find it. Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did you receive or were you familiar with our position regarding the treatment of abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in my statement -- not in my statement, during a conversation I said that there were cases where individual Muslims and Serbs wanted to have their mutual contracts certified regarding exchanges of houses and apartments, but that we declined due to the situation, which was a war and the state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever receive any instructions in August? Did the municipality receive it? You were still there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until the end of August, but I don't recall this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is hardly legible. I can't make things out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday at page 90, lines 20 through 23 of the transcript, the witness was still being cross-examined on the matter of contracts. The first five lines on page 91 and the bottom of page 90. [In English] I don't have the e-court on my ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now can we look at D15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that Renovica is not a village. Can you tell us how many settlements comprise Renovica and who lives there? Is the population mixed or do the hamlets have their respective ethnic compositions?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Renovica was a local commune and that there were some Serbs living there who, when the policemen in Renovica were injured, left the territory of Renovica. I don't know how many hamlets there are, but quite a lot and they all comprised the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who were the Serbs injured or killed by?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the policemen or the people who fled?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policemen were attacked by Muslims. The Muslims attacked and killed two policemen and wounded five. That was right at the start. After that, the Serbs were fearful and they withdrew from there leaving their property behind in the territory of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So do you recall this piece of news? Is this what you mentioned, the ambush on a police patrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that was the operation. Goran Kablar was killed then and Rade Tosic. Many others were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you changed positions, did you stay in Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still resided there in the weekend home of Hajrudin Somun who was a member of Alija Izetbegovic's Presidency. After the Dayton Accords he called me and told me, "Mr. Cvoro, I heard you live in my weekend home" -- sorry, this is very important. It is very important. He came and had a look at his weekend home and started to cry, saying, "Is it possible that you kept it all intact?" He wanted to go even further and turn to the media, thanking me personally. At first he was informed that his weekend home was among the first houses to be torched. Later he said, "Mr. Cvoro, you are a better person than I am because you preserved something that I may not have if I were in your place." He said that in the weekend home he even found a last paper issue he had read back then. And since I don't want to be singled out, I wanted to say that many Serbs kept Muslim property safe in the very same way in the territory of Pale municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Serb authorities take any part in the destruction of mosques or did they incite and encourage such destruction?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unaware of that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another question. You mentioned that the influx of refugees and the events in the theatre of war had a great impact on the atmosphere in Pale. In early June, before Muslims began requesting to be allowed to leave, did anything drastic happen resulting in concerns among their population? Did something take place in terms of combat?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The soldiers of the VRS from Pale municipality were obliged to supply food and other necessities to the soldiers who were detained in Zlovrh near Han Pijesak. They set off but never reached their destination --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Objection, objection. This is a rehashing of material that's in the statement that, in any event, didn't arise from cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Partially yes, partially no --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you not touch upon that issue, showing the Muslims' arrival or something like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I obviously in cross touched on issues raised by the statement, but now the witness is returning to repeating precisely what's in the statement. I can look at it, I believe it's paragraph 3 or 2, but I'll find you precisely where that's referenced. So if that's how the accused wants to use his time, I guess that's okay with the Prosecution; but I felt an obligation to bring that to the attention of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger is correct, Mr. Karadzic. Just -- you don't -- you should not just rehabilitate your examination-in-chief during your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, can you tell us what aspect of the cross are you seeking to have clarified by this question in re? Can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution allegations that the Muslims did not leave voluntarily but that they were forced by someone. I want to tackle what is not mentioned in the statement, which is the occurrence that all events in the environment and the goings-on in the theatre of war --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- including atrocities had an impact on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If we have to continue, I think we have to excuse Mr. Cvoro for the moment, but I take it you're done already.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, could you take off your headphones for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Were you through, Dr. Karadzic? Were you through with your answer to me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Only one -- yeah, yeah. There was one drastic incident that hadn't been mentioned in statement and that was very decisive about the further development. So I just wanted one question to ask him what happened on 10th of June and I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger, do you wish to comment on this at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- paragraph 4 relates a series of events that the witness indicated took place and that, according to him, caused fear of retaliation and security, et cetera, and that were the prompting factors, according to him, for the Muslims to leave. During the course of my examination, I directed the witness's attention and the Court's attention to factors beyond those. It seems to me -- that is, to factors regarding pressure on Muslims directly in Pale and forcible actions to get them to leave. It seems to me that the issue of whether or not there were actions in other theatres of war or whether VRS soldiers were killed, et cetera, et cetera, was not directly challenged and this is simply adding to that if -- the witness had a chance in his statement to provide his information on that, he did. And, by the way, I should mention that the specific incident that seems to have been referred to in the -- when Dr. Karadzic began the lead-up to the question that prompted this objection seems specifically to be in the statement. So it's -- again, I -- you know, I think it's a matter of efficiency more than anything else. I don't see that this is anything other than an effort to augment paragraph 4 with some additional incident that the accused thinks is significant but that the witness didn't think was significant enough to put in his statement. I don't believe that's an efficient use of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber does not think that question you were going to put arises from the cross-examination, so I would like you to move on to another topic. Yes, Mr. Cvoro, you can take -- you can wear your headphones again. Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, do you remember this huge funeral and do you remember that after that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- I put a ban on such mass funerals?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That -- that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's leading and it's in contravention of the Court's decision about 10 seconds before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I relinquished the questions related to the 10th of June. I only wanted to ask how the people were buried and if he knew that, in the aftermath, I put a ban on such burials. But if this is not admissible, then I'm all right with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's move on. And if you start your question with "do you remember," that's usually leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvoro, in what way did you bury those 45 soldiers at Pale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO CVORO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was personally involved in the burial of the 46 soldiers at Pale. Half of them were buried on one day and the other half on the following day. On the second day of the funeral, but also on the first day as well because many fighters from Pale lost their lives, even some of the Muslims - and I saw them personally - were standing by and expressing sympathy with what had happened to their neighbours and friends. The second day of the funeral, the presence of a large number of inhabitants and combatants at Pale was abused in the sense that the Muslim forces, considerable Muslim forces, attacked a defence line at Trebevic. This was hand-to-hand fighting. Many who were in front of the church ran to their houses, picked up their weapons, and unfortunately many of them never returned. An additional 12 VRS fighters were killed as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvoro, for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Unless my colleagues have questions for you, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Cvoro. On behalf of the Chamber I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we take an early break or continue with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless there's an objection, we'll have a break now for half an hour and resume at ten to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the witness take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Tieger, that you have an attorney who appears for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. And for observing. Yes, Bronagh McKenna is with the Karadzic team and will be leading a witness shortly and will be introducing herself to the Court personally. Thank you for noticing, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Pejic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D6812 in e-court. We have the version in the English language, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. Dr. Pejic, have you given a statement to the Defence team and is that the statement that you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have given a statement, and on this occasion I would just like to make one correction, if possible, for the statement to be completely accurate, and I'm referring you to page 8.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the version in Serbian, page 8.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's no Serbian version -- B/C/S version uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the paragraph number, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this paragraph it says that I met Dr. Karadzic in 1994. It should be corrected to read that it was in early 1995. This correction was made on the basis of a newspaper article in which I saw that this happened on the 12th of January, 1995. I don't know if that is relevant, but I think that a correction is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. As for the rest of your statement, does it accurately reflect everything you said?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it reflects everything and is written down exactly as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation and I'm also asking you to do the same because both of us speak the same language. Have you signed the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I signed it on the 2nd of December, 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to ask you today the same questions that the Defence team put to you, would your answers basically be the same?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would, only perhaps I would have elaborated my answers a little bit if I have an opportunity to speak live and in order to clarify some of the paragraphs, but the essence would remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm going to read the summary -- sorry, Your Excellency. May I offer this package for admission? Only maybe I will put some of the documents to the witness live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I noted that you have uploaded the redacted version and I take it you are tendering one document? Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. We're tendering 1D10016 and we would ask for permission to add it to the Rule 65 ter list because we didn't have the witness's statement at the time we made that list, so we hadn't included it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Given the Trial Chamber's ruling that this paragraph is of some relevance to the indictment, we have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give the numbers to the statement and the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D06802 [sic] receives number D2538, Your Honours. And document 1D10016 receives number D2539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'm going to read the summary of Dr. Pejic's statement in English. [In English] Milan Pejic served in the JNA from February until December 1994 [sic] at the Officers' Medical School in Belgrade. Following this, Dr. Pejic worked at the Hadzici health --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, not 1974 but 1975.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, we'll correct this. [In English] Following this, Dr. Pejic worked at the Hadzici Health Centre before moving to the ORL clinic at Kosevo Hospital - that means ear, nose, and throat - Kosevo Hospital in March 1979. Dr. Pejic became chief of the clinic in 1991. On March the 8th, 1992, Juka Prazina - a very famous criminal - was admitted to Kosevo Hospital and armed personnel belonging to the Green Berets controlled entry and exits to the clinic and checked ID papers. At that time everyone in Sarajevo felt insecure and many check-points were set up manned by unknown armed formations. Around March 1992, Republican Minister of Health, Dr. Ismet Lipa, issued a document ordering healthcare workers to report to the nearest healthcare institution and place themselves at its disposal in the event that the situation deteriorated still further and going to work as normal was not possible. In April 1992, a Crisis Staff was formed at the Kosevo Medical Centre. In the middle of April 1992, Dr. Milan Pejic attended a morning meeting and was asked to sign a pre-prepared text, in which was written that Dr. Radovan Karadzic was proclaimed a war criminal --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, perhaps after I have finished we can --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pejic has some intervention.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In mid-April you did not say that that was a meeting of experts, not the meeting of Crisis Staff. And I would like that to be put accurately.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Okay. So I'll repeat. In April 1992, a Crisis Staff was formed at the Kosevo Medical Centre. In middle of April of 1992, Dr. Milan Pejic attended a morning meeting at his own clinic and was asked to sign a pre-prepared text, in which was written that Dr. Radovan Karadzic was proclaimed a war criminal and that he should be stripped of the title of doctor and prohibited from working because of alleged sniping at the citizens of Sarajevo. As the local outpatient unit in Blazuj was unsuitable for the admission of patients requiring beds, Dr. Milan Pejic assisted in the creation of a temporary hospital in a holiday centre of the Zica armature factory. Everything done at this hospital was an example of people organising themselves due to a feeling of being under threat and of looming danger and was done without prompting and certainly not by any external directive. On April the 22nd, 1992, following a fierce assault of Muslim forces on Ilidza from a health care facility, 12 or 13 citizens of the Serbian ethnicity were killed and 37 people wounded. They were admitted to the hospital, one being a recordist from the BBC in London. On May the 8th, 1992, Dr. Pejic was informed in a meeting that while employees of the clinical centre Kosevo were being transported to work by bus, they had been stopped by the Kosevo stadium by members of a group of armed people who wanted members of the Serbian ethnicity to be taken off the bus. This was prevented by Dr. Lutvo Hodzic. After this, Dr. Milan Pejic was not able to get to work owing to the escalation of the conflict and therefore he devoted all his capacity for work at the Zica hospital. The hospital received very small amounts of medicines and medical material. Every day he saw columns of various vehicles transporting aid for Sarajevo, and at the beginning they diverted a certain percentage of the resources but many were of no use to their hospital because of incompleteness and other reasons. The main source of supply for medicines and medical material was humanitarian assistance. At the beginning of December 1992 an agreement was reached which gave the hospital one-third of the oxygen bottles. They received five or six bottles, two of which were unusually heavy. A subsequent check established that one of the bottles contained gunpowder and there was some kind of detonator, fuses, in the other. The detonators were packaged in paper with "Kovina Visoko" written on it. UNPROFOR were informed and they denied being involved. A large number of wounded members of the VRS passed through the hospital as well as members of the HVO and Muslims. Further, a large number of civilians received treatment at the hospital during the war, both Serbs and other civilians who were the victims of snipers or shelling from the Muslim positions. Some of the witnesses, as it is said in statement, have been treated by the Dr. Pejic staff. And that's all for now. I don't have questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did I not order you to lead live about para 17?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I think we redacted everything, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think I said to you that it's a bit difficult to follow what 17 meant, so I want you to lead the witness in that regard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, if you have your statement in front of you -- actually, do you have it in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I kindly ask you to look at paragraph 17 and could you tell us what this means in essence, the maternity home in Betanija?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the then-clinical centre we had meetings of the Crisis Staff every morning. This Crisis Staff consisted of the directors of the clinics and the director of the clinical centre as a whole. At the time when this happened, what is referred to in paragraph 17, the Crisis Staff was chaired by Mr. Ismet Lipa, the then-minister of health. Now what was it that I wanted to say by this statement? I wanted to say that what happened later in relation to the new maternity ward, we called it Betanija and that was Dolina. It has to do with a TV programme that had to do with the presence of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and a dramatic programme stating that doctors cannot deliver babies at the new maternity ward. That was not true because the mentioned professor, Srecko Simic, who was head of the clinic for gynaecology and obstetrics, at this meeting on the 7th of May said that they had carried out all their work, or rather, transferred all of these activities to the old building in terms of gynaecology and obstetrics and that they're handing over the new building to the Crisis Staff. This programme was at some point in May, after the 20th of May, I think, it had to do with the conflict and the shelling of this new maternity building. I don't think that this programme was truthful and I think that it was actually aimed at different purposes. I am trying to say that some of the things that people on the other side did were not appropriate and did not correspond to the situation that then prevailed in Sarajevo. I don't know whether I've answered with sufficient clarity. I don't know if I should repeat this. Quite simply, I couldn't keep silent about this because I personally attended the meeting of the Crisis Staff on the 7th of May and with my very own ears I heard what Professor Srecko Simic asked for and I personally heard who was appointed to the team to carry out the hand-over of the building, the instruments, and the staff of this maternity clinic, which is actually part of the clinic for gynaecology and obstetrics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what is your objection with regard to this TV programme?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Well, look, as far as I can remember from this point of view now, the old gynaecology building was shown in that programme - the gentlemen don't know about it but you do. The old building had been renovated and is used again and all activities were carried out there. Obstetrics was there before and after that meeting. Now what the reason was I really don't know because I'm not a soldier, but then there was shooting, shelling. Now, was it from one side or both sides? And, inter alia, what was mentioned was the new maternity building, and in this TV programme the mentioned president of the then-Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Izetbegovic, appeared. There was a foreign official, there were doctors, and as far as I can remember, that was one of the reasons why some kind of sanctions were imposed. Now I don't know, was it sanctions that were imposed on Serbia? Whatever. I'm perhaps mistaken, but anyway that's the way it was. At any rate, this untruthful picture was portrayed as far as the new maternity building was concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, is this paragraph somewhat clearer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Doctor, is it your testimony that the new maternity home was never shelled by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot confirm or deny that because I was not present there at the time. By then I was no longer going to Kosevo. This is after I had stopped coming, but on television I saw this programme which dramatically portrayed the situation at the old maternity ward and that that was a consequence of the shelling of the new maternity home. Now, whether that really happened or not, I cannot confirm. But what I can confirm with certainty is that the late Professor Dr. Srecko Simic said that the new maternity building is not being used and that all the procedures regarding gynaecology and obstetrics are being carried out in the old building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. At this point in time I wouldn't have any further questions for Dr. Pejic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, as you have noted, most of your evidence in chief has been admitted in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead. Do go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, you said that the treated all patients, regardless of their nationality. And you said -- and you used Ramiz Mujkic as an example. How did Ramiz Mujkic come to be treated in the hospital? He didn't just walk into the hospital off the street, did he?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Heaven forbid. He was driven in some vehicle. He was brought in. He was wounded in the leg, either the left or the right one, I'm not sure. I don't know. His hygiene had been rather poor --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He was --

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: -- neglected, not to say that he smelled --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: -- the wound was -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, you've answered the question. He was brought into the hospital by a number of persons, including a military policeman. He was also taken from the hospital by a soldier and two military policemen, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Madam, as for Mr. Ramiz, we gave him all medical assistance possible --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Doctor -- Doctor --

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: -- I saw him the other day --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Doctor, can you pause there. My question was he left the hospital. He was also taken from the hospital by a soldier and two military policemen. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Well, I really cannot recall. It would be too much for me to ask me to remember what happened 20 years ago, but it was probably the way you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P2325, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Doctor, we see here hospital records from the Zica hospital in relation to the patient Ramiz Mujkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we go to the second page -- is that -- and the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that a hospital record with your signature at the bottom of the page or two-thirds of the way down the page? Does it say there Dr. Pejic --

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: We see a bit further down -- no, this is not my signature. MY name is typed out, though. At the time, we did not have such forms -- or did we? On the left side it was signed by Dr. Djulic. He was a dentist and he did some medical work, too, in terms of general medicine. I as head of the hospital was supposed to sign this where it says "head of hospital." Unfortunately I probably wasn't there when Ramiz was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So you don't recall him being taken to the Zravka [phoen] military prison?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Well, no, no, well, look --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document now.

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Pejic, I want to move on now. You said in your statement that Dr. Karadzic was basically a good person and a man who was good to his neighbours. I'd like to show you a short clip and then I will put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I can play Exhibit P02515, please. And the clip is from 1:55:45 to 1:58:28, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may while we're waiting. May I indicate the mistranslation on that medical documentation. In Serbian it says "zarobljeni" and in English it says "prisoner" and the difference is considerable in our language. It should state "prisoner of war."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We take it as a standing observation. So I don't think you have to repeat it every time. Thank you. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Registrar, if we could have the English translation of this exhibit on the screen, please, for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We cannot follow the video-clip? What -- how can we follow the video-clip if --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, apparently -- yes, Your Honour. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Reid's printing sufficient copies to give it to the interpreters' booths. If the usher could assist, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note that the transcript hasn't been uploaded in e-court either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's under 65 ter number 45177, Your Honour, A, 45177A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we are waiting for translations to be given to interpreters, I would just like to clarify one thing on the record. The version of the witness statement that was admitted is number 1D6812 and not 1D6802, as was mistakenly put on the record previously. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting, Ms. Sutherland, I don't find any transcript in that number either, 45177.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 45177A, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If everyone is ready, can we play the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: With sound.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "RK: We are determined ... our Assembly adopted, to get separated and we have separated and formed our state. But some changes have to happen in Sarajevo itself in a way that Serb areas go to Serbs in its entirety by means of political negotiations and talks; in the way that Serbian city will be formed and separated as a whole; in the way the former Sarajevo is transformed into two cities. It is our firm political will and decision, and if our neighbours and the international community as well wish to peacefully solve this problem, then they have to realise that genuine Serbian areas in the territory of Sarajevo have to go to Serbs and a city will be formed there, a city which should have -- which should be a shelter and home for about 200.000 Serbs and continually develop on an urban principle and on centre-towards-periphery principle." Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones be switched off. Thank you. [Voiceover] "We have a completely clear vision about it. And we will try to make it true. We have entirely accepted and welcomed your regulation in the declaration so that the rest of Sarajevo can stay in Republika Srpska if it wants to, as there are economic and historical, national and all other conditions and reasons; and if not, then we will make some arrangements to enable those who do not want to live with us to connect to their territory in some way. If our neighbours do not show enough understanding, we will decide for ourselves how big Srpsko Sarajevo, Serb Sarajevo, will be and what will be in Srpsko Sarajevo. And then Sarajevo is a city and the city in Republika Srpska because all the land Sarajevo is situated on is Serbian and all the surroundings are Serbian, and if they do not want to come to a quick solution, the whole of Sarajevo will be Serbian in the end." Interpreter's note: The quality of soundtrack is very poor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Doctor, were you able to follow what Mr. Karadzic has said in this video-clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is the microphone on now? Well, I could follow but I don't know when it was that Dr. Karadzic was speaking, what the date was, what the year. In paragraph 30 of my statement I said that my knowledge about Dr. Karadzic is indirect, not direct; and what I heard from colleagues is what I wrote in this statement. I am not talking about the period before the war and after the war. I mean, I hope this is clear from my statement, what this refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably you pre-empted Ms. Sutherland's question. I just asked whether you heard it. Ms. Sutherland, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? I have to intervene as far as the translation is concerned. In line 15 on page 45, it was said "only," "exclusively" through negotiations. And here it says in the translation "in its entirety," but I said "ekskluzivno" which is "only," "exclusively" through negotiations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have a transcript and in that regard I would like to -- I would like the CLSS to take a look into it. And having said that, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic was saying this at the time that he visited Ilidza at the same time that he came to the Zica hospital. But this doesn't sound like Dr. Karadzic cares much for his Muslim and Croat neighbours, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN PEJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
